data.name: Baruchon
data.long_meaning: The name Baruchon is derived from the Hebrew word 'baruch' which means 'blessed'. In the Bible, the name Baruch is given to various individuals, including a scribe who lived during the Babylonian exile and a son of Abimelech. In Christian tradition, Baruch is revered as a saint and is known for his faith and dedication to God. The name carries a deep spiritual significance, reminding us of the blessings and grace bestowed upon us by God.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's blessings and grace.

historical_references.reference: Baruch was a scribe and probably the secretary of the prophet Jeremiah. The Book of Baruch, also known as the Fourth Book of Ezra, was included in the Vulgate and the Septuagint but was not included in the Hebrew Bible. It was believed to have been written between 515 BCE and 516 BCE, during the Babylonian exile.
historical_references.context: Babylonian exile, Scribe, Jeremiah's secretary, Author of the Book of Baruch

historical_references.reference: Baruch Ben Neriah is mentioned in the Old Testament as a friend and companion of the prophet Jeremiah. He is known for his faithfulness to Jeremiah and for his encouragement of him during difficult times. Baruch is also credited with preserving the prophecies of Jeremiah during the Babylonian exile.
historical_references.context: Companion of Jeremiah, Preserved Jeremiah's prophecies during Babylonian exile
